# Derived by tools/asynccheck.py - do not edit by hand; run it with --accept.
# Each line is a global written after an await with no check between the two.
# Being here means somebody read it and decided it is safe. It should shrink;
# when it grows, the run says so and the commit says which of the two reasons.
# The 24 lines added on 22 August 2026 are the options pages, the backgrounds and the content
# scripts, which this check had never read - `sidepanel.html` was its whole subject, 9 of the 32
# shipped scripts. The content scripts were *opened* and not read: both are wrapped in an IIFE, so
# every function in them is indented by two, and this tool looked at column zero - 0 of 32 and 0 of
# 19, over 42 awaits, in the two files that do the authenticated fetching. Corrected 22 August 2026,
# and the headline now prints how much of its own subject it read. What follows was true of the
# scopes it *did* read: none is the defect this tool is for, since
# that defect is «the *workspace* changed under an operation» and none of those scopes has one. What
# they have is one load overtaking another, which the options pages answer with `markOwn`/`dirty`.
# Recorded rather than exempted, so a *new* one there is still a finding.
#
# The three in `rebuildTree` are cache invalidations after the permission await: dropping a cache in
# the workspace you have left costs a rebuild, and the publication two lines below is guarded.
#
# What it cannot see is in the docstring: an arrow-function body, including the onChanged handler
# where both panels rewrite the folder handle after an await.
